Situation1: A family member has a significant event they want to share with everyone.
Situation2: A winter storm is slowing traffic while the passenger must catch an international flight
Story: The snow was coming down in thick, heavy flakes, making the city look like a shaken snow globe. I gripped the steering wheel, glancing at the anxious passenger in my back seat. He kept checking his watch, muttering about missing his international flight. My job was clear: get him to the airport safely and on time, no matter the weather. But my phone buzzed with a message from my daughter—my grandson had just won his school’s science fair, and the family was gathering to celebrate. I could almost hear his excited voice, see his proud smile. I was supposed to be there, to cheer him on, to be the grandparent he counted on. But here I was, crawling through icy streets, torn between the responsibility of my job and the pull of my family. The weight of both expectations pressed on me, and I felt the ache of being needed in two places at once, knowing I could only choose one.
